title: NVIDIA's filed guarantee book stays under $25B of a reported $250B by Q4 2027
body:
The Wall Street Journal put a figure on NVIDIA's role in OpenAI's Ohio expansion on Monday: NVIDIA is in talks to guarantee roughly $250 billion of financing behind OpenAI's lease of a ten-gigawatt campus at Piketon, on the former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant site, developed by SoftBank-backed SB Energy, with a separate negotiation covering as much as $350 billion to finance the NVIDIA chips that would fill it. Reuters could not independently confirm the report, pricing, duration, collateral and repayment are all undisclosed, and neither company commented. The prediction is that the $250 billion stays a negotiating notional. Through the close of Q4 2027, NVIDIA quantifies no guarantee — in a 10-Q, a 10-K, an 8-K, or an announcement it publishes itself — whose stated maximum potential future payments reach $25 billion, one tenth of the reported figure.

The gap is structural rather than a judgment about whether the talks are real. A guarantee is written against a draw schedule, and a draw schedule follows construction. The campus's first phase is 800 megawatts targeting 2028, eight percent of ten gigawatts, and eight percent of $250 billion is $20 billion — that is the size of instrument a lender can actually put to work inside this window. The $250 billion describes what the whole campus would cost to finance if every phase gets built and every phase gets guaranteed on the same terms, which is an outcome, not a signed document. NVIDIA's own book makes the scale problem concrete: its disclosed guarantee exposure is reported at $3.5 billion with $712 million in escrow, and it closed its January fiscal year with $62.6 billion in cash. A $250 billion maximum would be more than seventy times the first number and roughly four times the second, a contingent obligation several times NVIDIA's cash on hand, carried in a commitments-and-contingencies note against OpenAI, which holds no investment-grade rating. That missing rating is the whole reason a chip vendor is being asked to stand behind its customer's rent — lenders would be underwriting NVIDIA's credit instead of OpenAI's — and it is also why the obligation gets staged rather than granted whole.

The market supplied the incentive in the same session. NVIDIA closed roughly 5% lower on the report, AMD about 5% and Teradyne about 4%, with the VanEck Semiconductor ETF off more than 2%, while a slide of more than 8% in crude left the Dow up 0.51% and the S&P 500 flat; the selling was specific to the vendor-financing story rather than to the tape. Three days earlier NVIDIA had signed a letter of intent with SK Group valued above $500 billion, covering a two-gigawatt SK Telecom AI factory and long-term AI-memory supply from SK hynix. A company whose shares fall when it is reported to be standing behind OpenAI's rent has every reason to make the committed number small, staged and late, and to keep the chip-financing track separate from the lease track so that neither carries the other's notional into the same footnote.

The counting rule is the filed number, not the reported one. More journalism about the size of the talks does not falsify this, and neither does a definitive agreement announced with a $250 billion headline, unless NVIDIA itself puts its own maximum exposure at or above $25 billion in a document it files or publishes. A phase-scoped guarantee disclosed at $15 billion or $20 billion is consistent with the prediction rather than against it: the claim is about the order of magnitude that reaches NVIDIA's accounts, not about whether NVIDIA becomes a credit provider to OpenAI. On this evidence it is becoming one. What the prediction settles, if it holds, is which of the two numbers was ever real. The headline notional and the filed notional are different objects, the distance between them is roughly a factor of ten, and the first phase of a campus that does not energize until 2028 is the only part of it a guarantee can attach to before the end of 2027.

reasoning.because: The Wall Street Journal reports NVIDIA in talks to guarantee ~$250B behind OpenAI's Piketon lease
reasoning.given: Financing follows build phases; the first phase is 800 MW of 10 GW and terms are still unsigned
reasoning.so_that: Any guarantee NVIDIA actually books is phase-scoped, an order of magnitude below the campus-wide headline
reasoning.landing: By Q4 2027 NVIDIA has quantified no guarantee at or above $25 billion
reasoning.plain_language: NVIDIA may promise to cover OpenAI's rent, but the figure it actually puts in its own accounts will be far smaller than the headline.

summary: The Wall Street Journal reports NVIDIA in talks to guarantee about $250 billion behind OpenAI's ten-gigawatt Ohio lease, against a guarantee book reported at $3.5 billion. Financing follows phases, and phase one is 800 megawatts. By Q4 2027 NVIDIA quantifies no guarantee reaching $25 billion.
